description: Compute the Erdős–Selfridge plus or minus class of one supplied rational prime using the recursive prime-factor class recurrence.

contract.definition: For a supplied rational prime p and direction s in {-1,+1}, let N=p+s. The class is max({1} union {1+class_s(q): q is a distinct prime factor of N and q>3}). Thus a prime has class 1 when all prime factors of its selected neighbor are 2 or 3. Classes are defined recursively on smaller primes.
contract.input_encoding: [p,s], where p is the prime and s=1 selects p+1 while s=-1 selects p-1
contract.overflow_behavior: Every selected neighbor is at most 100001. Distinct factorization and all loop products use divisors no larger than the square root of that neighbor. Recursive factor primes are smaller than p; the class is at most 17 for this bound, so all intermediate and output values fit signed i64.
contract.recurrence_order: Only distinct prime factors greater than 3 contribute; prime powers are reduced to one occurrence.

input.validation_order: Reject null input, lengths outside 1..3, non-exact two-word frames, primes outside 2..100000, directions other than -1 or +1, and composite p before class recursion.

output.meaning: Positive Erdős–Selfridge class for the selected p±1 direction, or -1 for invalid input.

workspace.accounting: Native ports use scalar factorization state and recursive calls only. Every recursive factor is at most (p+1)/2 for p>3, giving fewer than 18 active levels for p<=100000; 4096 bytes conservatively covers those frames and scalar bookkeeping. Caller-owned input and ABI call metadata are excluded. No heap or variable-sized native array is used.

complexity.primary_time: Recursive distinct factorization by trial division; worst-case bounded by the factor scans over the decreasing factor tree
complexity.independent_time: O(p log log p) sieve plus bottom-up SPF factorization through p
complexity.independent_space: O(p) tables in the Python reference
